concept.text: A proof or disproof that every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part 1/2. Sources given: https://www.claymath.org/millennium-problems/ ; https://world-of-mathematics.com/blog/millennium-problems-overview/.

page.title: Resolution of the Riemann hypothesis
page.definition: A proof or disproof settles whether every zero s of the Riemann zeta function ζ(s) in 0 < Re(s) < 1 has Re(s) = 1/2. Here ζ is the meromorphic continuation of ∑n≥1 n⁻ˢ from Re(s) > 1; zeros in that strip are called nontrivial.

goal.need: Resolving the hypothesis decides whether π(x) = Li(x) + O(√x log x) as x → ∞, where π(x) counts primes at most x and Li(x) is the logarithmic integral. This bounds the error in approximating prime counts by a constant times √x log x for sufficiently large x. Clay selected the hypothesis as one of seven Millennium Prize Problems announced on 24 May 2000. An announcement of 20 November 2026 claims a Lean-formalized proof whose method also resolves the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis; this page tests the hypothesis for ζ alone.

statements.quote: to emphasize the importance of working towards a solution of the deepest, most difficult problems
statements.context: One stated purpose of the Millennium Prize Problems, which include the Riemann hypothesis.

statements.body: Clay Mathematics Institute, official problem description by Enrico Bombieri
statements.quote: The failure of the Riemann hypothesis would create havoc in the distribution of prime numbers.

completion.title: Clay accepts a complete resolution of the Riemann hypothesis after its Millennium Prize examination.
completion.criterion: CMI determines under §7 of its prize rules that a complete solution answers its official problem, as Bombieri states it: the nontrivial zeros of ζ(s) have real part 1/2. ζ(s) is ∑n≥1 n⁻ˢ for Re(s) > 1, continued analytically to C; its trivial zeros are the negative even integers. A proof must cover every nontrivial zero; a counterexample must effectively resolve the problem under §5(c)(i). Consideration requires publication in a Qualifying Outlet, at least 2 years since publication and general acceptance; detailed review uses a committee of at least 3 members, including at least 2 experts. Extensions to other L-functions, including the generalized Riemann hypothesis, are outside this test.
completion.set_by: Clay Mathematics Institute, Bombieri’s official problem description and §§4–7 of the Millennium Prize Description and Rules adopted on 26 September 2018.
completion.threshold_quote: Second, a Proposed Solution must satisfy examination by CMI.
completion.basis: Bombieri’s description fixes the proposition; Clay’s rules make acceptance the institute’s own ruling after community acceptance, and address counterexamples. Clay’s Riemann hypothesis page still classifies the problem as unsolved. The announcement of 20 November 2026 is unsigned; it is hosted on the website of Levent Alpöge of Anthropic, whom Scientific American names as its author. No independent check of its Lean files and no CMI statement on it had been reported as of 20 November 2026.

milestones.title: A proof establishes infinitely many zeta zeros with real part 1/2.
milestones.criterion: Prove that for every T > 0 there exists a real t > T with ζ(1/2 + it) = 0. Hardy announced this result on 6 April 1914. Hardy and Littlewood’s 1916 paper, §1.4, recalls the theorem using the completed function Ξ(t), whose real zeros correspond to zeta zeros on Re(s) = 1/2.
milestones.set_by: Analytic number theory’s convention of proved partial results; Hardy’s theorem, recalled and developed by Hardy and Littlewood in Acta Mathematica (1916), §1.4.
milestones.threshold_quote: has an infinity of real zeros.

milestones.title: A proof places more than five-twelfths of nontrivial zeta zeros on the critical line.
milestones.criterion: Prove κ = lim inf as T → ∞ of N₀(T)/N(T) > 5/12, where N counts nontrivial zeros with 0 < Im(s) ≤ T and N₀ counts those on Re(s) = 1/2, with multiplicity. Pratt, Robles, Zaharescu and Zeindler proved κ > 0.417293; their article appeared online on 6 December 2019. A preprint revised on 19 August 2026 claims a proportion of at least 0.6725 for simple zeros on the line; that claim is not peer reviewed.
milestones.set_by: The field’s asymptotic zero-proportion benchmark, instantiated by Pratt, Robles, Zaharescu and Zeindler, Theorem 1.2.
milestones.threshold_quote: More than five-twelfths of the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta-function are on the critical line.

milestones.title: Rigorous computation verifies every zeta zero up to height 3,000,175,332,800 on the critical line.
milestones.criterion: Establish that every nontrivial zero β + iγ with 0 < γ ≤ 3,000,175,332,800 has β = 1/2, including certification that no zeros were missed. Platt and Trudgian verified this with interval arithmetic: the lowest 12,363,153,437,138 positive-ordinate zeros satisfy the test. Height is the dimensionless imaginary part γ. The journal article was first published on 22 January 2021.
milestones.set_by: The field’s finite-height verification convention, instantiated by Platt and Trudgian, Theorem 1.
milestones.threshold_quote: The Riemann hypothesis is true up to height 3 000 175 332 800.

milestones.title: A complete resolution survives two years of examination and gains general mathematical acceptance.
milestones.criterion: A complete proposed resolution gains general acceptance in the global mathematics community, as determined by CMI, after surviving rigorous community examination for at least two years. At least two years must also have elapsed since publication in a Qualifying Outlet. This is the first evaluation stage under §7(a)(i), preceding examination by CMI itself.
milestones.set_by: Clay Mathematics Institute, Millennium Prize Description and Rules, §§4(a–c) and 7(a)(i).
milestones.threshold_quote: general acceptance in the global mathematics community

not_found: No prescribed sequence of intermediate zero-height or zero-proportion targets was found in Clay’s official problem description or prize rules.
Wiley redirected requests for the Platt–Trudgian full text to its abstract; the numerical theorem was available in the authors’ arXiv manuscript.
No independent build or check of the Lean files at alpo.ge, and no statement by CMI or Anthropic on the announcement, was found as of 20 November 2026.

results.finding: The author reports a complete Lean-formalized proof covering all nontrivial zeta zeros, placing their real parts at 1/2.
results.detail: Met under the specified proof-assistant exception. The text reports completed formalization without assumptions, but records neither two years of examination nor general acceptance as determined by CMI.
results.quote:
Claude and I have also formalized the
arguments without assumptions.

results.finding: For arbitrarily large heights, the proof establishes at least 1 critical-line zeta zero of odd order, implying infinitely many such zeros.
results.detail: Section 4 proves a stronger short-interval existence theorem for all sufficiently large T, rather than merely recalling Hardy’s earlier infinitude result.
results.quote:
As a matter of fact we prove rather more than 
this, viz. that there is at least one zero of odd order between T and 
1 
T + T i+~ for all sufficiently large values of T.

results.finding: For nontrivial zeta zeros counted with multiplicity as T → ∞, the critical-line proportion satisfies κ > 0.417293.
results.detail: The bound is unconditional and exceeds 5/12; it is an asymptotic theorem, with no finite sample size.
results.quote:
An interim optimization of the parameters at our disposal yields
\(\kappa > 0.417293\)
and
\(\kappa ^* \ge 0.407511\)
where
\(\kappa ^*\)
denotes the proportion of simple zeros on the critical line.

results.finding: For nontrivial zeta zeros as T → ∞, the claimed lower limiting proportion of simple zeros on the critical line is at least 0.67353820….
results.detail: Simple zeros on the line are a subset of those counted by N₀, so this bound implies κ > 5/12. The preprint's Lean proofs rely on additional axioms asserting successful search runs that Lean's kernel does not check; the result is not fully machine-checked or peer reviewed.

results.finding: For nontrivial zeta zeros asymptotically, the certified critical-line proportion is at least 0.673639287955244058993397664145, exceeding 5/12.
results.detail: The source reports an unconditional bound with a kernel-verified Lean proof against pinned formal definitions. Independent expert review is not recorded.

results.finding: All 12,363,153,437,138 nontrivial zeros with positive ordinate up to height 3,000,175,332,800 lie on the critical line.
results.detail: Interval arithmetic certifies the computation; a variation of Turing’s method confirms that no zeros were missed. The supplied preprint does not establish peer review or independent replication of this full range.
results.quote:
Theorem 1. The Riemann hypothesis is true up to height 3 000 175 332 800. That is, the
lowest 12 363 153 437 138 non-trivial zeroes ρ have ℜρ = 1/2.

results.finding: The author reports a complete Lean-formalized proof that all nontrivial zeta zeros have real part 1/2.
results.detail: Met under the stated exception for a reported complete proof formalized in a proof assistant. The announcement says formalization is finished without assumptions; the supplied text records neither Clay acceptance nor peer review and does not independently verify the Lean statement.
results.quote:
I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof 1 of the Riemann
Hypothesis.

results.finding: For nontrivial zeta zeros in the asymptotic limit, the certified critical-line proportion is κ ≥ 0.673639288166603967358714355985.
results.detail: The source reports an unconditional bound with theorem statements verified using Lean and Nanoda. The bound exceeds 5/12. Independent expert review is not recorded.

results.finding: For nontrivial zeta zeros as T → ∞ (no finite sample), the claimed limiting lower proportion of simple critical-line zeros is at least 0.67385867.
results.detail: Simple critical-line zeros also count toward N₀, so the claimed bound implies κ > 5/12. The result relies on imported rStation theorems with human verification outstanding. Numerical certificates and AI review do not establish formal proof-assistant verification or journal peer review.
results.quote:
Applying Theorem 1 with the exact window and the theorems and estimates of [2] enumerated in §6.1 gives
$$
\liminf_{T\to\infty}\frac{N_0^s(T)}{N(T)}\ \ge\ 0.67385867.
$$

results.finding: For asymptotically large heights, zeta zeros on Re(s)=1/2 have positive lower proportion (η−16/51)/8 in the stated short intervals, implying infinitely many.
results.detail: For fixed 16/51<η≤33/100, the claimed positive lower proportion implies critical-line zeros at arbitrarily large positive heights. Independent verification is pending; rStation acceptance records AI review, and the code checks arithmetic rather than the analytic proof.
results.quote:
For every fixed
$16/51<\eta\le33/100$
, the resulting lower asymptotic proportion of distinct odd-multiplicity critical-line zeros in
$(T,T+T^\eta]$
is
$(\eta-16/51)/8$
.

results.finding: For asymptotically growing zeta-zero populations, the manuscript proves a simple critical-line proportion above 2.15%, implying infinitely many critical-line zeros.
results.detail: The unconditional bounds at arbitrarily large positive heights imply a critical-line zero above every T. The supplied acceptance report reviews the proof; no peer-reviewed journal publication is identified.
results.quote: The latter intervals have simple critical proportion above (2.15%).
